\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بخشیدن} (bakhshidan)}{بخشیدن (bakhshidan)}]{\fa{بخشیدن} (bakhshidan) — to forgive}

\label{lesson:FA-C221-bakhshidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to print, then the Persian for to photocopy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بخشیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{بخشیدن}} — \emph{bakhshidan} — \textquotedblleft{}to forgive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bakhshidan} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed: it continues Middle Persian \emph{baxš-}, \textquotedblleft{}to share out, to grant\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). Persian uses \textquotedblleft{}to grant\textquotedblright{} for forgiving.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{قهر} \fa{کردن} (qahr kardan)}{قهر کردن (qahr kardan)}]{\fa{قهر} \fa{کردن} (qahr kardan) — to fall out, to stop speaking to someone}

\label{lesson:FA-C221-qahr-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to photocopy, then the Persian for to forgive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{قهر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{قهر} \fa{کردن}} — \emph{qahr kardan} — \textquotedblleft{}to fall out, to stop speaking to someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{qahr kardan} pairs \emph{qahr}, borrowed from Arabic \emph{qahr}, \textquotedblleft{}force, wrath\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{q-h-r}, Lane), with the Persian verb \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do, to make\textquotedblright{}. \emph{kardan}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, is an inherited verb, from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB). Persian uses it for sulking and refusing to speak.
\end{cousinweb}
